messages:
sasha: Quick field notes from the anticipatory-decode probe on llm3-7b-quant (early bring-up). Posting short summary + config so we can decide canary/next steps.

sasha: TL;DR: solid median speedups, noticeable tail improvements, small but measurable quality regressions on knowledge-grounded QA. Some context below.

mohit: nice — numbers?

sasha: Baseline (4-bit quant, no anticipatory logic): p50=92ms, p95=240ms, QA EM=72.4%, hallucination=3.1%, token-cost=1.00x.

sasha: Anticipatory decode (3-bit quant + window=2, confidence threshold=0.65): p50=68ms (-26%), p95=188ms (-21%), QA EM=70.9% (-1.5pp), hallucination=4.0% (+0.9pp), token-cost=0.78x.

sasha: Key failure modes observed:
- hallucination uptick concentrated on long context fact-lookup where anticipatory picks a high-prob but wrong continuation and prefetches non-grounded tokens.
- KV-cache thrash if prefetch_margin_tokens set > 12 for short-turn dialogues.

sasha: Experiment config (what we ran):
```json
{
  "model_variant": "llm3-7b-quant-v1",
  "quant": "3-bit",
  "anticipatory_window": 2,
  "confidence_thresh": 0.65,
  "prefetch_margin_tokens": 8,
  "fallback_policy": "late_bind",
  "collect_prefix_logprobs": true
}
```

elaine: are those EM drops statistically significant across the eval split? also what split?

sasha: Eval sets: TruthBench-qa (5k examples) + DialogHelpfulness (3k human-rated). EM drop on TruthBench is ~1.5pp, p=0.02 (bootstrap). Dialog helpfulness avg rating down 0.06 on a 1-5 scale, not huge but visible on edge cases.

mohit: any ideas to reduce hallucination while keeping latency win?

sasha: Options we sketched:
- per-token confidence gating: only prefetch when predicted token logprob > threshold AND next-token entropy below X.
- selective anticipatory on non-fact domains (classify request intent first).
- hybrid fallback: if downstream grounding signal (RAG scores or citation mismatch) low, immediately invalidate prefetched tokens and fall back to full decode.

devon: Could we try anticipatory_window=1 + higher conf threshold to trade a bit speed for quality?

sasha: Yup. Quick sim shows w=1, conf=0.75 recovers ~0.9pp EM while keeping p50 ~ -18%. I'll run a 100k query sim to get stable estimates.

mohit: Also want p99 under bursty load — we only measured p95 in bench. Add a microburst test (100 reqs/sec for 30s).

sasha: Good call. Noted. I saw some tail spikes when multiple requests hit the same shard and prefetches forced KV eviction. Need to add jitter to prefetch start timestamps.

deploy-bot: canary started: route 10% internal traffic -> revision "ant-dec-v1" (origin: eng-ml/probe/6155555555) :rocket:

devon: we should only canary on internal/ci traffic first. don't expose to external customers until RAG/regression gates pass.

sasha: Agreed. Plan: canary internal 10% for 24h, collect logs into s3://redwood-inference/eng-ml/ant-dec/v1/6155555555/, run automated quality regression checks (TruthBench EM, hallucination detectors, helpfulness sample). If any regression > 1.0pp or hallucination delta > 0.5pp -> rollback.

elaine: add RAG-style prompts to the eval set; anticipatory decode might be more brittle there.

sasha: Will add. Also going to instrument prefix-logprob histograms and a small probe that computes "prefetch error" = cases where prefetched token != final emitted token (post re-decode).

mohit: actionable checklist from this thread?

sasha: 1) run w=1/conf=0.75 sim (sasha)
2) microburst p99 bench (mohit)
3) add RAG eval + run canary on internal only (devon)
4) instrument prefetch-error and prefix-logprob histograms (sasha)
5) if canary OK -> staged external canary 1% (ops)

devon: I'll own the canary gating and rollback automation.

elaine: sgtm. please post the first canary summary here when ready.

mohit: :thumbsup: thanks sasha, nice concise notes.

sasha: thanks team — pushing follow-ups to the eng-ml repo and will tag you all.
